predecessors.name: Kingdom of Kush
predecessors.text: the Nile 'from the 3rd cataract to south of Abu Hamed at Mograt Island', the Makurian core after Kush's collapse

successors.name: Kingdom of Makuria (Dotawo)
successors.text: Lower Nubia, ruled from Gebel Adda and Qasr Ibrim after the loss of Dongola in 1365: the kingdom as it stood in 1414

ledger.x: 347: Makuria rises on the Dongola reach after Kush's collapse.
962: Makurian forces hold Upper Egypt as far as Akhmim.
964: the Makurians withdraw from Upper Egypt; Egypt fell to the Fatimids in 969 and Ibn Salim al-Aswani visited Georgios III 'immediately afterward'.
1175: the Ayyubid raids end 'in 1175 at Adindan' and Qasr Ibrim returns to Makuria.

4 June 1276: 'Mashkouda was installed on the Makurian throne on 4 June 1276', after the Mamluks 'dispatched a large army on 20 January 1276' that 'met the Nubian army at Dongola, defeating it decisively'; the king 'had to swear an oath of fealty to Baybars, thus turning Makuria into a Mamluk vassal state' and 'was…
1316: Abdallah Barshanbu, the first Muslim king of Makuria, is installed by the Mamluks; he 'was slain in late 1317' and 'a mosque in the throne hall was attested in 1317'.
1365: Dongola falls in the civil war; the court flees to Gebel Adda.
1365: the court moves to Gebel Adda in Lower Nubia (infobox 'Gebel Adda (after 1365)'); Mamluk letters of 1367 went to Apakyre at Gebel Adda and to Shihab al-Din Majid at Qasr Ibrim.

1414: Cliopatria's 'Makuria' row ends and its 'Makuria Kingdom' row begins; the pages describe one continuous kingdom (Nazir dethroned 1397, the Banu Kanz expelled from Aswan 1412/3, Joel attested 1463, collapse 'probably in the late 15th century'), so this is a hand-over to the same state under a second slug, with…

wars.name: First Battle of Dongola
wars.outcome: Makurian victory: Uqba ibn Nafi's column of 20,000 horsemen reached Dongola, 'were beaten back, and Amr withdrew from Nubia'; no territorial change.

wars.name: Second Battle of Dongola
wars.outcome: Makurian victory: Abdallah ibn Sa'd 'laid siege to the city' with about 5,000 men and a catapult, suffered heavy losses and 'called off the siege in exchange for a pact', the Baqt (360 slaves a year against wheat, barley, wine, horses and linen), which…

wars.name: Makurian raids on Upper Egypt
wars.outcome: Raids on Kharga (951) and Aswan (956); in 962-964 Makurian forces reached Akhmim.

wars.name: Ayyubid invasion of Nubia
wars.outcome: Makurian pillage of Aswan in 1172; Turan-Shah took Qasr Ibrim in January 1173; 'Kurdish raids lasted two years, ending in 1175 at Adindan'.

wars.name: Mamluk–Makurian wars
wars.outcome: Mamluk raid to Dongola 1265; David sacked Aidhab 1272; the Mamluk army sent out on 20 January 1276 defeated Makuria at Dongola, and the Mamluks installed Mashkouda on 4 June 1276; Simamon held power by 1286 and Mamluk invasions followed in the late 1280s.

wars.name: Mamluk interventions and the Muslim kings
wars.outcome: Kudanbes usurped the throne in 1311; the Mamluks installed Barshanbu in 1316 (slain late 1317); the Kanz al-Dawla, arrested in Cairo and released, 'seized the Makurian throne' and two Mamluk expeditions against him failed, 'the last in 1324' (Banu Kanz page)…

wars.name: Makurian civil war and the fall of Dongola
wars.outcome: Dongola 'captured by the tribesmen and its king killed'; the court moved to Gebel Adda; a Mamluk expedition took the surrender of the Kanz al-Dawla at Qus in December 1365 and the Mamluks returned to Egypt early in 1366.

certainty.note: Every frontier approximate: the cataracts (third, then first) are the only fixed points; the Alodian frontier near Abu Hamed/al-Abwab is a reading of the pages.

The Egyptian frontier at Aswan/Philae is fixed in effect by the Baqt of 652, though the pages name no border point; the desert and Alodian frontiers stay soft; after 1365 the southern limit (Batn el-Hajar) is the researcher's.
